title: Arakhin 10
description: The mishna’s minimums and maximums in the Temple service: trumpet blasts, lyres and flutes, the twelve days the flute plays before the altar and who played it, and the Gemara’s days of full Hallel, followed by stories of Temple instruments that sounded best as they were first made.
topics: 🌙 “Lamp of Israel!”: Rabbi Shimon solves his father’s calendar puzzle
📯 Twenty-one to forty-eight blasts, or seven to sixteen: how Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis count tekia, terua, tekia
🎶 Two to six lyres, two to twelve flutes, and the twelve days the flute plays before the altar
🗓️ Eighteen days of full Hallel, twenty-one in the Diaspora
❓ Why not Shabbat, the New Moon, Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur, and why not Purim?
📖 The angels’ question: books of life and death are open
🪈 The reed flute from the days of Moses, the cymbal and the mortar: repairs that spoiled them
💧 The Siloam spring and the hydraulic organ that was not in the Temple

a1.he: וְעִיבּוּר שָׁנָה שְׁלֹשִׁים (אישתקד) [וְאִישְׁתָּקַד] עָשִׂינוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם מְלֵאִין, דַּל תְּלָתָא לְבַהֲדֵי תְּלָתָא וְקָם לֵיהּ בְּדוּכְתֵּיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל! כֵּן הָוֵה.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְלֹא מוֹסִיפִין עַל אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה.

a3.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁנֵי נְבָלִים, וְלֹא מוֹסִיפִין עַל שִׁשָּׁה. אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁנֵי חֲלִילִין, וְלֹא מוֹסִיפִין עַל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר, וּבִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה הֶחָלִיל מַכֶּה לִפְנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ: בִּשְׁחִיטַת פֶּסַח רִאשׁוֹן, וּבִשְׁחִיטַת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי, וְיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח, וּבְיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת, וּבִשְׁמוֹנַת יְמֵי הֶחָג. וְלֹא הָיָה מַכֶּה בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת, אֶלָּא בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל קָנֶה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקּוֹלוֹ עָרֵב; וְלֹא הָיָה מְחַלֵּק אֶלָּא בְּאַבּוּב יְחִידִי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְחַלֵּיק יָפֶה.

a4.he: וְעַבְדֵי כֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר; רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מִשְׁפַּחַת בֵּית פְּגָרִים וּבֵית צִיפְּרָא מֵעֶמָּאוּם הָיוּ מַשִּׂיאִין לַכְּהוּנָּה; רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: לְוִיִּם הָיוּ.

a5.he: גּמ׳: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשֶּׁבַע, וְלֹא יוֹסִיף עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.

a6.he: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: תְּקִיעָה תְּרוּעָה וּתְקִיעָה חֲדָא הִיא, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: תְּקִיעָה לְחוּד, וּתְרוּעָה לְחוּד, וּתְקִיעָה לְחוּד.

a7.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? כְּתִיב ״וּתְקַעְתֶּם תְּרוּעָה״, וּכְתִיב ״תְּרוּעָה יִתְקְעוּ״ (לָכֶם), שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: תְּקִיעָה תְּרוּעָה וּתְקִיעָה — חֲדָא הִיא. וְרַבָּנַן? הַהוּא לִפְשׁוּטָה לְפָנֶיהָ וּפְשׁוּטָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ הוּא דַּאֲתָא.

a8.he: וְרַבָּנַן מַאי טַעְמָא? דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְהַקְהִיל אֶת הַקָּהָל תִּתְקְעוּ וְלֹא תָרִיעוּ״, וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ תְּקִיעָה תְּרוּעָה וּתְקִיעָה חֲדָא הִיא, אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא עֲבֵיד פַּלְגָא דְּמִצְוָה? וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה — סִימָנָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.

a9.he: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אֵין בֵּין תְּקִיעָה לִתְרוּעָה וְלֹא כְּלוּם? כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. פְּשִׁיטָא!

a10.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אֲפִילּוּ כְּרַבָּנַן אָתְיָא, וּלְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר: שָׁמַע תֵּשַׁע תְּקִיעוֹת בְּתֵשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם — יָצָא. קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a11.he: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי! אִם כֵּן, מַאי ״וְלֹא כְּלוּם״?

a12.he: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה מַכֶּה בֶּחָלִיל וְכוּ׳. מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי? הוֹאִיל וְיָחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל.

a13.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר יָמִים שֶׁהַיָּחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל: שְׁמוֹנָה יְמֵי הַחַג, וּשְׁמוֹנָה יְמֵי חֲנוּכָּה, וְיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח, וְיוֹם טוֹב (הָרִאשׁוֹן) שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת; וּבַגּוֹלָה עֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד: תִּשְׁעָה יְמֵי הַחַג, וּשְׁמוֹנָה יְמֵי חֲנוּכָּה, וּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל פֶּסַח, וּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת.

a14.he: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּחַג דְּאָמְרִינַן כֹּל יוֹמָא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּפֶסַח דְּלָא אָמְרִינַן

b1.he: כֹּל יוֹמָא? דְּחַג חֲלוּקִין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹתֵיהֶן, דְּפֶסַח אֵין חֲלוּקִין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹתֵיהֶן.

b2.he: שַׁבָּת דַּחֲלוּקָה בְּקָרְבְּנוֹתֶיהָ, לֵימָא! לָא אִיקְּרִי ״מוֹעֵד״.

b3.he: רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ דְּאִיקְּרִי ״מוֹעֵד״, לֵימָא! לָא אִיקַּדַּישׁ בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״הַשִּׁיר יִהְיֶה לָכֶם כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג״ — לַיְלָה הַמְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג טָעוּן שִׁירָה, וְשֶׁאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג אֵין טָעוּן שִׁירָה.

b4.he: רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים, דְּאִיקְּרוֹ ״מוֹעֵד״, וְאִיקַּדּוּשׁ בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה, לֵימָא! מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ.

b5.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְפָנֶיךָ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים? אָמַר לָהֶן: אֶפְשָׁר, מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא הַדִּין, וְסִפְרֵי חַיִּים וְסִפְרֵי מֵתִים פְּתוּחִין לְפָנָיו, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְפָנַי?

b6.he: וְהָא חֲנוּכָּה דְּלָא הָכִי וְלָא הָכִי, וְקָאָמַר! מִשּׁוּם נִיסָּא. פּוּרִים דְּאִיכָּא נִיסָּא, לֵימָא! אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה עַל נֵס שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ.

b7.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וַהֲרֵי יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, דְּנֵס שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ הוּא, וְאָמְרִינַן הַלֵּל! כִּדְתַנְיָא: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאָרֶץ — הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל הָאֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה, מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְאָרֶץ — לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה.

b8.he: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הִיא הַלֵּילָאּ. רָבָא אָמַר: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם ״הַלְלוּ עַבְדֵי ה׳״ — וְלֹא עַבְדֵי פַרְעֹה, הָכָא ״הַלְלוּ עַבְדֵי ה׳״ — וְלֹא עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ? אַכַּתִּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן!

b9.he: וּלְרַב נַחְמָן דְּאָמַר: קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הִיא הַלֵּילָאּ, הָתַנְיָא: מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְאָרֶץ לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁגָּלוּ חָזְרוּ לְהֶיתֵּירָן הָרִאשׁוֹן.

b10.he: לֹא הָיָה מַכֶּה בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת וְכוּ׳. פָּתַח בְּחָלִיל וּמְסַיֵּים בְּאַבּוּב. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ חָלִיל הַיְינוּ אַבּוּב, וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״חָלִיל״? דַּחֲלֵי קָלֵיהּ.

b11.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַבּוּב הָיָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, חָלָק הָיָה, דַּק הָיָה, שֶׁל קָנֶה הָיָה, וּמִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה הָיָה. צִוָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ וְצִיפּוּהוּ זָהָב, וְלֹא הָיָה קוֹלוֹ עָרֵב, נָטְלוּ אֶת צִפּוּיוֹ וְהָיָה קוֹלוֹ עָרֵב כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה. צִלְצוֹל הָיָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת הָיָה, וְהָיָה קוֹלוֹ עָרֵב, וְנִפְגַּם, וְשָׁלְחוּ חֲכָמִים וְהֵבִיאוּ אוּמָּנִין מֵאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וְתִקְּנוּהוּ, וְלֹא הָיָה קוֹלוֹ עָרֵב, נָטְלוּ אֶת תִּיקּוּנוֹ וְהָיָה קוֹלוֹ עָרֵב כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה.

b12.he: מַכְתֶּשֶׁת הָיְתָה בְּמִקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת הָיְתָה, וּמִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה הָיְתָה, וְהָיְתָה מְפַטֶּמֶת אֶת הַבְּשָׂמִים, נִתְפַּגְּמָה וְהֵבִיאוּ אוּמָּנִין מֵאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וְתִיקְנוּהָ, וְלֹא הָיְתָה מְפַטֶּמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה, נָטְלוּ אֶת תִּיקּוּנָהּ וְהָיְתָה מְפַטֶּמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה.

b13.he: אֵלּוּ שְׁנֵי כֵלִים נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ מִמִּקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן, וְנִתְפַּגְּמוּ וְלֹא הָיָה לָהֶם אֲרוּכָה, וַעֲלֵיהֶם אָמַר דָּוִד: ״נְחוֹשֶׁת מְמוֹרָט״, ״נְחוֹשֶׁת מְמוֹרָק״, וַעֲלֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וּכְלֵי נְחֹשֶׁת מוּצְהָב שְׁנַיִם חֲמוּדוֹת מִזָּהָב״.

b14.he: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד שָׁקוּל כִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁל זָהָב, וְחַד אָמַר: שְׁנֵיהֶם שְׁקוּלִין כְּאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב. תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: שְׁנֵיהֶם שְׁקוּלִין כְּאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב.

b15.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: שְׁנִיִּים הָיוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁנַיִם״, אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״שְׁנַיִם״ אֶלָּא ״שְׁנִיִּים״.

b16.he: תָּנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: שִׁילוֹחַ הָיָה מְקַלֵּחַ מַיִם בִּכְאִיסָּר, צִוָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהִרְחִיבוּהוּ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְרַבּוּ מֵימָיו, וְנִתְמַעֲטוּ, וְחָזְרוּ וּמִיעֲטוּהוּ וְהָיָה מְקַלֵּחַ מַיִם, לְקַיֵּים מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חָכָם בְּחׇכְמָתוֹ וְאַל יִתְהַלֵּל גִּבּוֹר בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ״.

b17.he: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הִרְדַּוְלִים לֹא הָיָה בְּמִקְדָּשׁ. מַאי הִרְדַּוְלִים? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַבְלָא גּוּרְגְּדָנָא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקּוֹלוֹ עָרֵב וּמְעַרְבֵּב אֶת הַנְּעִימָה.

b18.he: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַגְרֵיפָה הָיְתָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,

messages.text: Continued from 9b: a baraita tells that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi once made nine months of a year deficient, and yet the new moon was sighted in its proper time. His son Rabbi Shimon suggested: perhaps last year was a leap year…

…and the month that was intercalated, added for the leap year, was thirty days, and last year we turned two months that are generally deficient into full months, which meant that it had eight full months instead of the usual six. Consequently, remove from consideration the three months that were made deficient this year corresponding to the three extra months that were made full last year, and the moon is restored to its place, i.e., it is properly aligned with the months.

notes.he: הרי לך א' מלא ואשתקד עשינו שניהן מליאים מרחשון ואייר והרי לך שלשה מלאין יותר על כסדרן הלכך כי חסרה השתא לבהדייהו שלשה קם ליה בדוכתיה:
notes.en: And the intercalated month of the year was thirty: there you have one full month. And last year we made both of them full, Marḥeshvan and Iyyar: there you have three full months beyond the regular order. Therefore, when three are made deficient now, against them, the moon stands in its place.

notes.he: ועדפו ב' ימים ויום העבור היה שלישי והיינו כרב הונא דאמר דח' מלאין עבדינן:
notes.en: And last year we made both of them full: so two days were left over, and the day added in the intercalation was the third. This accords with Rav Huna, who said that we make eight full months.

notes.he: [דל מהני ט' חסירין תלת לבהדי הנהו תלת הילכך קם ליה בדוכתי' ונראה בזמנו]:
notes.en: [Remove three of these nine deficient months against those three; therefore it stands in its place, and the moon was seen in its time.]

messages.text: @Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Lamp of Israel! Indeed, so it was.

notes.he: שאתה מאיר עיני חכמים:
notes.en: Lamp of Israel: for you light up the eyes of the Sages.

notes.he: כלומר אתה הוא מאיר [כנר] לישראל שידעתה לכוין הדבר:
notes.en: Lamp of Israel, so it was: that is, you are the one who gives light [like a lamp] to Israel, for you knew how to work the matter out.

messages.text: Mishna

No fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts are sounded daily in the Temple, as each day three blasts were sounded for the opening of the gates in the morning, nine for the daily morning offering, and nine for the daily afternoon offering, totaling twenty-one.

notes.dh: (שייך למתני') אין פוחתין מכ"א תקיעות במקדש בכל' יום
notes.he: ומפרש בסוכה (דף נג:) שלשה לפתיחת שערים ותשע לתמיד של שחר שהיו הלוים אומרים שירה בשעת נסכים והיה בו ג' פרקים לכל פרק תקעו והריעו ותקעו:
notes.en: (This belongs to the mishna.) No fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple each day: it is explained in Sukkah (53b): three for the opening of the gates, and nine for the daily morning offering, for the Levites would sing at the time of the libations, the song had three sections, and for each section they sounded a tekia, a terua and a tekia.

notes.dh: [מתני' שתי הלחם אין נאכל פחות משנים ולא יותר על שלשה
notes.he: כיצד נאפה מערב עצרת ונאכל בעצרת לשנים הוי יום ב' חל להיות אחר שבת נאכל לשלישי:
notes.en: [Rabbeinu Gershom here returns to lines of the mishna on 8b.] Mishna: The two loaves are eaten no sooner than the second day and no later than the third. How so? They are baked on the eve of Atzeret [Shavuot] and eaten on Atzeret, which is the second day; if the festival falls right after Shabbat, they are eaten on the third.

notes.he: לחם הפנים נאפה מע"ש ונאכל לשבת הבאה לתשעה חל יום טוב להיות בע"ש נאכל לעשר ב' ימים של ר"ה נאכל לי"א שאין אפייתו דוחה לא את השבת ולא את י"ט:
notes.en: The showbread is baked on Friday and eaten on the following Shabbat, on the ninth day. If a festival falls on Friday, it is eaten on the tenth; if the two days of Rosh HaShana [fall before Shabbat], it is eaten on the eleventh, since its baking overrides neither Shabbat nor a festival.

notes.he: מפורש במס' שבת פרק ר' אליעזר דמילה:
notes.en: A minor is not circumcised sooner than the eighth day: this is explained in tractate Shabbat, in the chapter Rabbi Eliezer of circumcision.

notes.dh: אין פחות מכ"א תקיעות במקדש ולא מוסיפין על מ"ח
notes.he: מפרש במס' סוכה בהחליל]:
notes.en: No fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple, and no more than forty-eight: this is explained in tractate Sukkah, in the chapter HeḤalil.

messages.text: And no more than forty-eight are ever sounded on a single day. This would occur on the Friday of Sukkot, when they would sound an additional twelve blasts during the ritual of drawing the water for the water libation; nine for the additional offerings; three to signal the population to cease their work before Shabbat; and three more to mark the beginning of Shabbat.

notes.he: מתני' כ"א תקיעות ומ"ח תקיעות מפרש להו במס' סוכה בפ' החליל (סוכה דף נג:):
notes.en: Mishna. Twenty-one blasts and forty-eight blasts: these are explained in tractate Sukkah, in the chapter HeḤalil (Sukkah 53b).

messages.text: When accompanying their song with instruments, the Levites do not use fewer than two lyres and do not use more than six.

notes.he: לשני לוים:
notes.en: From two lyres: for two Levites.

notes.he: לא אתפרש טעמא:
notes.en: And not more than six: no reason is given.

notes.he: פירש"י לא איתפריש טעמא אין פוחתין מב' חלילים ולא מוסיפין על י"ב כנגד י"ב יום שחליל מכה:
notes.en: (This belongs to the mishna.) And not more than six: Rashi explained that no reason is given. No fewer than two flutes and no more than twelve: corresponding to the twelve days on which the flute plays.

notes.dh: אין פוחתין מב' נבלים ולא מוסיפין על ששה
notes.he: לא איתפרש לן מ"ט ששה. [ב' נבלים ולא פחות דהכי אמר בסיפא דפירקין וב' נבלים וצלצל]:
notes.en: No fewer than two lyres and no more than six: the reason for six is not explained to us. [Two lyres and no fewer, for so it says in the latter clause of our chapter: “and two lyres and a cymbal.”]

notes.he: היינו עץ עשוי כמין נפה עגול [של עץ] ופורס עליה מיכן [ומיכן] הכרס של כבש [תמיד] כדתנן במסכת (תמיד) [קנים] מעיו לנבלים היינו הכרס בני מעיו לכינורות היינו הדקין והיה מניחו לייבשו ואח"כ מכה על הכרס ומשמיע קול גדול:
notes.en: Nevel [lyre]: a round wooden frame like a sieve, over which is stretched, on this side [and that], the stomach of the lamb [of the daily offering], as we learned in tractate (Tamid) [Kinnim]: “its innards for lyres,” that is the stomach; “its intestines for harps,” that is the thin ones. He would leave it to dry, and afterward strike the stomach, and it would make a great sound.

notes.he: ואיכא דאמרי נבל הרפא בלע"ז:
notes.en: And some say: a nevel is a harpa [a harp] in the vernacular.

messages.text: When flutes are played, they do not use fewer than two flutes and do not use more than twelve.

notes.he: חליל קלמייל"ש בלע"ז:
notes.en: From two flutes: ḥalil (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: אם היו רוצין היו עושין י"ב כנגד י"ב ימים שהחליל מכה לפני המזבח:
notes.en: And not more than twelve: if they wished, they would use twelve, corresponding to the twelve days on which the flute plays before the altar.

notes.he: ב' חלילים לא איתפרש לן מ"ט ב':
notes.en: Two flutes: the reason for two is not explained to us.

notes.he: כנגד י"ב (כהנים) [לוים] העומדים על הדוכן דאמר לקמן:
notes.en: And no more than twelve: corresponding to the twelve (priests) [Levites] who stand on the platform, as is said below.

notes.he: פיפא:
notes.en: Ḥalil: pipa [a pipe, in the vernacular].

messages.text: And there are twelve days during the year when the flute plays before the altar: At the time of the slaughter of the first Paschal offering, on the fourteenth of Nisan; and at the time of the slaughter of the second Paschal offering, on the fourteenth of Iyyar; and on the first festival day of Passover; and on the festival of Shavuot; and on all eight days of the festival of Sukkot.

notes.he: שהיו נקבים בחליל ומכה באצבעו על הנקב להנעים את הקול:
notes.en: Plays [makkeh, literally “strikes”]: for there were holes in the flute, and he would strike the hole with his finger to make the sound pleasant.

notes.he: בי"ד בניסן שהיו קורין ההלל בעזרה בשעת שחיטה כדאמרינן בתמיד נשחט (פסחים סד.):
notes.en: At the slaughter of the first Paschal offering: on the fourteenth of Nisan, when they would read the Hallel in the Temple courtyard at the time of the slaughter, as we say in the chapter Tamid Nishḥat (Pesachim 64a).

notes.he: מזמר בכח לפני המזבח:
notes.en: The flute plays [makkeh]: it plays forcefully before the altar.

messages.text: And one would not play with a copper flute; rather, one would play with a flute of reed, because its sound is more pleasant.

notes.he: היינו חליל ובגמרא מפרש הכי:
notes.en: Abuv: that is a ḥalil, and the Gemara explains it so.

notes.he: קנה:
notes.en: Abuv: a reed.

messages.text: And one would conclude the music only with a single flute, because it concludes the music nicely.

notes.he: מסיים אלא באבוב יחידי כשהיה מגיע לסיום הנעימה היה האחד מן החלילים מאריך לאחר שתיקת האחר שזהו חילוק יפה יותר משיסיימו שניהם כאחד. חילוק היינו סיום שמחלק בין נעימה לנעימה. ובשעת הקרבה היה שיר זה והיו הלוים משוררים בפה את ההלל באותן י"ב ימים והחלילים מחללים ובשאר ימים היו נבלים וצלצל וכינורות והשיר היה אותו שיר המפורש בר"ה (דף לא.) אחד בשבת לה' הארץ ומלואה וכל המזמור ובשני גדול ה' ומהולל וכן כולם:
notes.en: And one would conclude [meḥalek] only with a single flute: when they reached the end of the melody, one of the flutes would draw out its sound after the other fell silent, for that is a more beautiful ending than if both ended together. Ḥilluk means the ending, which divides one melody from the next. This music was played at the time of the offering: on those twelve days the Levites would sing the Hallel with their mouths while the flutes played. On the other days there were lyres, a cymbal and harps, and the song was the one set out in Rosh HaShana (31a): on the first day of the week, “The earth is the Lord’s, and all that it holds,” the whole psalm; on the second, “Great is the Lord and much acclaimed”; and so for all of them.

notes.dh: לא היה מחלק אלא באבוב יחידי
notes.he: כלומר שבסוף השיר [הזה] היה מאריך בקול האבוב יותר משאר מיני זמר ובו היה מפסיק השיר מפני שקולו ערב ומחלק ומפסיק יפה:
notes.en: And one would conclude only with a single flute: that is, at the end of [this] song he would draw out the sound of the abuv longer than the other kinds of music, and with it he would end the song, because its sound is pleasant and it concludes and ends well.

messages.text: The Temple musicians were slaves of priests; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: אותם המכים בחליל:
notes.en: And they were slaves of priests: those who played the flute.

notes.he: משאר אומות אותן מזמרין בכלי שיר:
notes.en: And they were slaves of priests: from the other nations; those who played the musical instruments.

messages.text: The musicians were not slaves, but Israelites from the family of the house of Pegarim and the family of the house of Tzippara from the city of Emaum, and their lineage was sufficiently pure that they would marry their daughters to members of the priesthood.

notes.he: שם המשפחה:
notes.en: Beit HaPegarim and Beit Tzippara: the names of the families.

notes.he: שם המקום:
notes.en: From Emaum: the name of the place.

notes.he: כהנים היו נושאין בנותיהן שישראלים מיוחסין היו:
notes.en: And they would marry into the priesthood: priests would marry their daughters, for they were Israelites of established lineage.

notes.he: יש ספרים שגורסין בית הפגריס בסמ"ך ויש שגורסין בית הפגרים במ"ם וכן כתוב בתוספתא (פ"א) ופסוק (ירמיהו לא) העמק הפגרים:
notes.en: Some texts read Beit HaPegaris, with a samekh, and some read Beit HaPegarim, with a mem; and so it is written in the Tosefta (chapter 1), and the verse (Jeremiah 31) has “the valley of the corpses [pegarim].”

notes.he: ישראל היו ומיוחסין ממשפחת בני פגריס וציפריא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei says: they were Israelites of established lineage, from the family of the house of Pegaris and Tzippara.

notes.he: מאותו מקום:
notes.en: And they were from Emaum: from that place.

messages.text: They were Levites.
Gemara
The mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda,
messages.quote: No fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts are sounded daily in the Temple

notes.he: דקחשיב כ"א תקיעות ומ"ח תקיעות דלא כר' יהודה דמתני' קא חשיב לכל תקיעה ולכל תרועה באנפי נפשה ואין לך כל תרועה שאין תקיעה פשוטה לפניה ולאחריה ורבי יהודה לא קא חשיב תקיעה ותרועה ותקיעה אלא חדא הרי לך כ"א דתנא דידן ז' לר' יהודה ומ"ח דתנא דידן ט"ז לרבי יהודה:
notes.en: Gemara. The mishna, which counts twenty-one blasts and forty-eight blasts, is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: for our mishna counts each tekia and each terua by itself, and there is no terua without a plain blast before it and after it; while Rabbi Yehuda counts a tekia, a terua and a tekia as only one. So you have: the twenty-one of our tanna are seven for Rabbi Yehuda, and the forty-eight of our tanna are sixteen for Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: One may not blow fewer than seven blasts, and one may not blow more than sixteen blasts.

notes.he: לרבי יהודה דאמר ליכא תקיעות כי אם שבעה משום דקר"ק חשיב תקיעה אחת והא דאמר בשבת פרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לה:) שהיו תוקעין ערב שבת ששה תקיעות כדי לבטל העם מן המלאכה לא הוי אלא תרתי אליבא דרבי יהודה דקחשיב לקר"ק תקיעה אחת אלא ו' נקט אליבא דרבנן וחשבינן קר"ק בשלשה תקיעות:
notes.en: One may not sound fewer than seven: for Rabbi Yehuda, who says there are only seven blasts, since he counts tekia-terua-tekia as one blast. And as for what it says in Shabbat, in the chapter Bameh Madlikin (35b), that they would sound six blasts on Shabbat eve to stop the people from work: according to Rabbi Yehuda, who counts tekia-terua-tekia as one blast, those are only two. Rather, it said six according to the Rabbis, and we count tekia-terua-tekia as three blasts.

notes.he: תקיעות בכל יום ולא יותר על ט"ז. דהיינו שליש מדתנן במתניתין ר' יהודה סבר תקיעה תרועה ותקיעה חדא הלכך קאמר ז' דהיינו כ"א דמתניתין דסבר כל חד וחד לחודי וי"ו דר' יהודה היינו מ"ח דמתניתין:
notes.en: He may not sound fewer than seven blasts each day, nor more than sixteen: that is, a third of what we learned in our mishna. Rabbi Yehuda holds that a tekia, a terua and a tekia are one; therefore he says seven, which are the twenty-one of our mishna, which counts each one by itself; and the sixteen of Rabbi Yehuda are the forty-eight of the mishna.

messages.text: With regard to what principle do the tanna of the mishna and Rabbi Yehuda disagree?

Rabbi Yehuda holds: A series of blasts consisting of tekia, terua, tekia is counted as one unit. And the Rabbis hold: A tekia is counted as a discrete unit and a terua is also counted as a discrete unit, and the final tekia is again counted as a discrete unit. They agree with regard to the sequence and the number of the blasts; their disagreement is only with regard to how the blasts are tallied.

messages.caption: Same blasts, two tallies: the Rabbis count each tekia and terua, Rabbi Yehuda counts each tekia–terua–tekia as one, so 21 and 48 become 7 and 16.

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda? As it is written in the verse: “And you shall sound [utkatem] a terua”, and it is written: “A terua they will sound [yitke’u]”. Conclude from the fact that the Torah uses a verb from the root tekia when referring to a terua that a tekia, terua, and tekia together constitute one unit.

verse.he: וּתְקַעְתֶּם תְּרוּעָה וְנָסְעוּ הַמַּחֲנוֹת הַחֹנִים קֵדְמָה׃ וּתְקַעְתֶּם תְּרוּעָה שֵׁנִית וְנָסְעוּ הַמַּחֲנוֹת הַחֹנִים תֵּימָנָה תְּרוּעָה יִתְקְעוּ לְמַסְעֵיהֶם׃
verse.en: But when you sound short blasts, uncertain. the divisions encamped on the east shall move forward; and when you sound short blasts a second time, those encamped on the south shall move forward. Thus short blasts shall be blown for setting them in motion,

notes.he: אלמא לתרועה קרי תקיעה ולתקיעה תרועה:
notes.en: And you shall sound [utkatem] a terua: evidently it calls a terua a tekia, and a tekia a terua.

notes.he: קרי לתרועה תקיעה וקרי לתקיעה תרועה דכתיב תרועה יתקעו ש"מ דחדא היא]:
notes.en: And you shall sound a terua: it calls a terua a tekia, and it calls a tekia a terua, as it is written “a terua they shall sound”; conclude from this that it is one.

messages.text: And how do the Rabbis interpret these verses? They explain that these verses come to teach that each terua blast is accompanied by a plain blast, a tekia, preceding it and another plain blast following it.

notes.he: דמהכא נפקא פשוטה לפניה דכתיב ותקעתם והדר תרועה ופשוטה לאחריה דכתיב (במדבר י׳:ו׳) תרועה והדר יתקעו ולעולם כל חדא מצוה באנפי נפשה:
notes.en: For a plain blast before it and after it: for from here we derive a plain blast before it, as it is written “and you shall sound [utkatem]” and then “terua,” and a plain blast after it, as it is written (Numbers 10:6) “terua” and then “they shall sound [yitke’u].” And in fact each one is a mitzva by itself.

messages.text: And what is the reasoning of the Rabbis? As it is written: “And when congregating the people you shall sound a tekia and shall not sound a terua”. And if it enters your mind that a series of tekia, terua, and tekia are considered one unit, would the Merciful One say to perform only half a mitzva? Rather, each sound constitutes a separate mitzva.

verse.en: while to convoke the congregation you shall blow long blasts, not short ones.

messages.text: And how does Rabbi Yehuda explain this verse? That single tekia mentioned in the context of congregating the people was blown merely as a signal to the people to assemble, not for the purpose of fulfilling a mitzva, which, in Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion, always comes in units of three sounds.

notes.he: לסימן שיקהלו ולאו לשום מצוה:
notes.en: Merely a signal: a sign that they should assemble, and not for any mitzva.

notes.he: ההוא תתקעו ולא תריעו לסימנא בעלמא הוי להקהיל משום הכי סגיא בחדא. אבל למצוה [ועבודה חשיב] תקיעה תרועה ותקיעה חדא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda: that “you shall sound a tekia and not a terua” is merely a signal to assemble; therefore one blast suffices. But for a mitzva [and the service, he counts] a tekia, a terua and a tekia as one.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is that which Rav Kahana said?
There is to be no pause between a tekia and a terua at all, but rather they are sounded in one continuous series of blasts.

notes.he: שלא ישהא ויפסיק בין פשוטה שלפניה לתרועה ובין התרועה לפשוטה שלאחריה אלא בבת אחת סמוכות זו לזו:
notes.en: And not at all: that he should not delay and pause between the plain blast before and the terua, or between the terua and the plain blast after it; rather, all at once, close to one another.

notes.dh: אין בין תקיעה לתרועה ולא כלום
notes.he: ומסיק דאתא כרבי יהודה דקאמר קר"ק חדא תקיעה וה"נ לרבנן דאסור להפסיק התקיעות ומכאן נראה לר' דאסור להפסיק בין שברים לתקיעות דהא מספקא לן [אי] גנוחי גנח וילולי יליל בהדי הדדי ולכך אנו עושים שברים ותרועה בהדי הדדי בחד תקיעה מספק ואסור להפסיק ביניהן ואם נאנס בתרועה ולא יכול לעשות מפני קוצר רוחו או מפני שום אונס יחזור לשברים והודה לו רבי מכאן משמע דאסור להפסיק בין תקיעה לתקיעה והא דאמרינן בשבת (שם) שהיו מפסיקין [דאמרינן] התקיעה הראשונה היתה כדי לבטל העם שבשדות שנייה להבטיל העיר וחנויותיה כו' שאני התם כיון דתקנום כן כדי להיות כל אחת ואחת סימן לדבר אחד לאו הפסק קחשיב ליה:
notes.en: There is no pause between a tekia and a terua at all: the Gemara concludes that this follows Rabbi Yehuda, who says tekia-terua-tekia is a single blast; and so too according to the Rabbis it is forbidden to pause between the blasts. From here it seemed to Rabbi [a Tosafist; the name is abbreviated] that it is forbidden to pause between the shevarim and the [terua]: for we are unsure whether [the terua is] groaning or wailing together, and so, out of doubt, we sound shevarim and terua together as one blast, and it is forbidden to pause between them. And if he was prevented during the terua and could not complete it, because of shortness of breath or some other constraint, he goes back to the shevarim; and Rabbi [likewise abbreviated] agreed with him. From here it is implied that it is forbidden to pause between one blast and the next. As for what we say in Shabbat (35b), that they would pause, where we say the first blast was to stop the people in the fields, the second to stop the city and its shops, and so on: there it is different, for since they instituted them so that each one is a sign for a different matter, it is not counted as a pause.

notes.he: דכיון דחדא היא אין מפסיק ביניהן כלום:
notes.en: There is no pause between a tekia and a terua at all: since it is one, he pauses nothing between them.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this statement? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.
messages.quote: There is to be no pause between a tekia and a terua at all

notes.he: דאמר חדא מצוה נינהו ולא בעי אפסוקי:
notes.en: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: who says they are a single mitzva and need no pause.

messages.text: Isn’t that obvious? Why was it necessary to point this out?

It is not obvious that Rav Kahana’s statement is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda. Lest you say that Rav Kahana comes to teach his halakha even in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and that he is coming to exclude only the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan,

notes.he: והאי אין בין לאו דיעשה סמוכות כל כך אלא שלא ישהה בינתיים יותר מדאי:
notes.en: Even in accordance with the Rabbis: and this “no pause between” would not mean that they must be so close together, only that he should not wait too long in between.

notes.he: והאי דקאמר ולא כלום לאו דוקא הוא אלא לאפוקי מדרבי יוחנן קאמר דכולי האי לא מפסיק קאמר אבל פורתא מצי מפסיק כרבנן דאמרי דתרי הוא קמ"ל דלא מפסיק כלום וכר' יהודה:
notes.en: Even the Rabbis: [lest you say that] this “not at all” is not precise, and it is said only to exclude Rabbi Yoḥanan, meaning he should not pause that long, though he may pause a little, in accordance with the Rabbis, who say they are two. [The Gemara] teaches us that he does not pause at all, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: If one heard nine blasts in nine different hours on the day of Rosh HaShana, despite the considerable gap between them, he has fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: דאמר גבי ר"ה שמע תשע תקיעות שלש של מלכיות וג' של זכרונות וג' של שופרות בתשע שעות ששהה שעה בין כל אחת ואחת יצא:
notes.en: And to exclude Rabbi Yoḥanan: who says regarding Rosh HaShana that if one heard nine blasts, three for Malkhuyot, three for Zikhronot and three for Shofarot, in nine hours, waiting an hour between each one, he has fulfilled his obligation.

messages.text: One might have thought that Rav Kahana meant only that there should not be such long gaps between the sounds. Therefore, the Gemara teaches us that Rav Kahana’s ruling is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as he does not allow any pause at all between the shofar blasts.

And how do you know that this was Rav Kahana’s intent? One can say it is indeed so, that Rav Kahana holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis and he merely excludes the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: דכדרבנן מצי לאוקומה:
notes.en: And say it is indeed so: that it can be established in accordance with the Rabbis.

messages.text: If so, what is the meaning of the phrase “at all” when Rav Kahana said that there is no pause between a tekia and a terua at all? This phrase indicates that Rav Kahana does not allow even a slight pause between blasts, which is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.
messages.quote: no pause between a tekia and a terua at all

notes.he: משמע כלל לא יפסיק:
notes.en: And not at all: this implies he should not pause at all.

notes.he: האי משמע דלא מפסיק כלל. אלמא משום דחדא הוו]:
notes.en: If so, what is “not at all”? This implies that he does not pause at all; evidently, because they are one.

messages.text: § What is different about these days enumerated in the mishna that the flute is played before the altar specifically on those occasions?
messages.quote: twelve days during the year when the flute plays before the altar

messages.text: They are unique, since these are the days on which the individual completes the full hallel.

notes.dh: הואיל והיחיד גומר בהם את ההלל
notes.he: בשחיטת פסח גומר בהם את ההלל:
notes.en: Since the individual completes the Hallel on them: at the slaughter of the Paschal offering one completes the Hallel. [A printed gloss adds that it should read: “but on the other days of Passover one does not complete it.”]

notes.he: (וב' ימי שחיטת הפסח אין גומר בהן את ההלל) כדאמרינן התם במסכת פסחים לא הגיע לאהבתי מפני וכו' אלמא דגומרין בהן את ההלל:
notes.en: [The printed text has here, in parentheses: “and on the two days of the slaughter of the Paschal offering one does not complete the Hallel.”] As we say there in tractate Pesachim: “they had not yet reached ‘I love’ [Psalms 116] because…”; evidently one completes the Hallel on them.

messages.text: There are eighteen days a year on which the individual completes the full hallel: The eight days of the festival of Sukkot, including the Eighth Day of Assembly; and the eight days of Hanukkah; and the first festival day of Passover; and the festival day of Assembly, i.e., Shavuot.
messages.lead: As Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:

notes.he: שמונה ימי חנוכה לא חשיב במתני' משום דליכא קרבן:
notes.en: The eight days of Hanukkah: the mishna does not count them, because there is no offering on them.

notes.he: הא דלא חשיב ערב פסח דאז הוו להו י"ט משום דלא הוי אלא במקדש לא חשיב ליה:
notes.en: Eighteen days: the reason it does not count the eve of Passover, which would make nineteen, is that [that Hallel] is only in the Temple; so it does not count it.

messages.text: And in the Diaspora, where a second day is added to each Festival due to uncertainty over the precise date, there are twenty-one days: The nine days of the festival of Sukkot; and the eight days of Hanukkah; and the first two festival days of Passover; and the two festival days of Assembly, i.e., Shavuot.

notes.dh: י"ח ימים שהיחיד גומר בהן את ההלל
notes.he: פי' ובשאר ימים אין אומרים אותו כלל דליכא לפרושי בשאר ימים אין גומרין אותו אבל קורין אותו בדילוג מדקאמר ר"ח איקרי מועד לימא משמע דסובר דאין אומרין בר"ח כלל וכן הא דקאמר מאי שנא בחג דאמרינן ובפסח דלא אמרינן משמע דאין חובה לאומרו כלל בר"ח ובפסח וכן משמע בהך דמסכת תענית (דף כח:) רב איקלע לבבל חזינהו דקרו הלילא בר"ח קסבר לאפסוקינהו כיון דשמע דקמדלגי אמר מנהג אבותיהם בידיהם משמע שרב היה סבור שלא היו אומרים אותו כלל וא"כ ודאי מה שאנו אומרים אותו אינו אלא מנהג בעלמא ואינו חובה כמו בי"ח ימים ומ"מ אומר ר"ת דצריך לברך עליו דכך משמע הך דסבר לאפסוקינהו (דכיון) שמברכין עליו דאל"כ מיד שראה רב שלא ברכו לפניו מיד היה יכול להבין שלא היה חובה אלא מנהג אלא ש"מ שברכו וכן משמע מהך דריש פ"ב דברכות (דף יד:) דקאמר רבא הילכתא שמונה עשר ימים שהיחיד גומר בהן ההלל בין פרק לפרק פוסק באמצע הפרק אינו פוסק ימים שאין היחיד גומר בהן ההלל אפילו באמצע הפרק פוסק ואם אין מברכין עליו מאי הפסקה איכא בדבר ותו מפני רשות נמי יפסיק ועד כאן לא איבעיא ליה אלא מפני היראה ומפני הכבוד ולא דמי להאי דקאמר פרק לולב וערבה (סוכה דף מד:) אמנהגא לא מברכינן ה"מ טלטול דמנהג כמו ערבה אבל אקריאה דמנהג מברכין שפיר והא דקאמר התם בפ"ד דתענית (דף כח:) תנא יחיד לא יתחיל ואם התחיל גומר פי' יחיד אין צריך להתחיל ואם התחיל גומר ובדילוג משמע דציבור חייבין היינו ממנהג בעלמא וק"ק רב דסבר לאפסוקינהו התניא הכא דציבור חייבין לקרותו וגם יחיד נמי גומר כשהתחיל ור"ח פי' יחיד לא יתחיל בברכה ואם התחיל בברכה גומר ומ"מ נקוט (דרבינו שמשון) [דר"ת] בידך דטוב לברך ליחיד נמי בתחילה דנהי דודאי אין מחוייב לאמרו מ"מ מאחר שמזקיק עצמו לכך אין זה ברכה לבטלה כמו שהנשים מברכות על נטילת לולב שאינו לבטלה אע"פ דפטורות מ"מ הם רשאות ליטלו ואין זה ברכה לבטלה. פסק:
notes.en: In brief: Eighteen days on which the individual completes the Hallel: that is, on other days it is not said at all. One cannot explain that on other days one does not complete it but reads it with skipping, since the Gemara says “the New Moon is called an appointed day; let us say it,” implying that on the New Moon it is not said at all; likewise “what is different about the Festival, that we say it, and Passover, that we do not say it” implies there is no obligation at all on the New Moon or on [the rest of] Passover. So too in Ta’anit (28b): Rav came to Babylonia, saw them reciting Hallel on the New Moon and thought to stop them; when he saw they were skipping, he said, “They hold to the custom of their fathers.” This implies Rav thought it is not said at all, so what we say is only a custom, not an obligation as on the eighteen days. Even so, Rabbeinu Tam says one must bless over it: Rav thought to stop them, which implies they were blessing (otherwise, seeing no blessing, he would have understood at once that it was only custom); and in Berakhot (14b) Rava rules that on the eighteen days one may pause between sections but not in the middle of a section, while on days when the individual does not complete it one may pause even in the middle; if no blessing were said, what pause would matter? And then he could pause even for a voluntary matter, yet the question there was only about pausing out of fear or out of respect. This is unlike Sukkah (44b), “over a custom we do not bless”: that refers to a custom of handling, like the willow, but over a reading that is a custom one does bless. As for Ta’anit (28b), “an individual should not begin, but if he began he completes it”: it means an individual need not begin, and if he began he completes it, with skipping; this implies the community is obligated, out of custom. A small difficulty: how could Rav think to stop them, when it is taught there that the community must read it and an individual too completes it once he has begun? Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained: an individual should not begin with a blessing, but if he began with a blessing he completes it. In any case, hold to the view of Rabbeinu Tam that it is good for an individual too to bless at the start: although he is certainly not obligated to say it, since he takes it upon himself it is not a blessing in vain, just as women bless over taking the lulav and it is not in vain, since although they are exempt they may take it. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.caption: The mishna’s twelve days of the flute beside Rabbi Yoḥanan’s eighteen days of full Hallel, and twenty-one in the Diaspora.

messages.text: What is different about the festival of Sukkot, that we say hallel every day, and what is different about Passover, that we do not say hallel…
…every day, but only on the first day?

The days of the festival of Sukkot are distinct from one another with regard to their additional offerings, as the number of bulls offered changes each day of Sukkot (see Numbers 29:12–38). Since each day is unique, the full hallel is recited on each day. By contrast, the days of Passover are not distinct from one another with regard to their additional offerings (see Numbers 28:24), and therefore the full hallel is recited only on the first day, which is the first day on which the additional offerings for a Festival are sacrificed.

notes.he: דפרי החג מתמעטין והולכין:
notes.en: The days of the Festival are distinct in their offerings: for the bulls of the Festival keep decreasing.

notes.he: פרי החג]:
notes.en: [Their offerings are distinct: the bulls of the Festival.]

messages.text: On Shabbat, which is also distinct from the other days of the week with regard to its additional offerings, let us say hallel.

notes.he: משאר ימי השבוע לימא הלל:
notes.en: Shabbat, whose offerings are distinct from the other days of the week: let us say Hallel.

messages.text: Shabbat is not called an appointed day in the Torah, and hallel is recited only on days that are referred to in the Torah as appointed days (see Leviticus 23:4), which are days of rejoicing.
On the New Moon, which is called an appointed day, let us say hallel.

notes.he: דכתיב (איכה א׳:ט״ו) קרא עלי מועד ובפ"ד דמסכת תענית (דף כט.) תמוז דההוא שתא מלויי מליוה דכתיב קרא עלי מועד:
notes.en: The New Moon is called an appointed day [mo’ed]: as it is written (Lamentations 1:15), “He proclaimed a mo’ed against me”; and in the fourth chapter of tractate Ta’anit (29a): Tammuz of that year was made full, as it is written, “He proclaimed a mo’ed against me.”

notes.he: ליגמר ביה הלל בגמרא במסכת שבועות [דף י.] קרא עלי מועד. תמוז דההוא שתא עבורי עברוה:
notes.en: The New Moon, which is called an appointed day: let us complete the Hallel on it. See the Gemara in tractate Shevuot (10a): “He proclaimed a mo’ed against me”: Tammuz of that year was made full.

messages.text: The New Moon is not sanctified with regard to the prohibition against the performance of labor, and hallel is recited only on a day that is sanctified, as it is written: “You shall have a song as in the night when a festival is sanctified”, which indicates that a night that is sanctified as a Festival, which includes a prohibition of labor, requires song, but one that is not sanctified as a Festival does not require song.

verse.he: הַשִּׁיר יִהְיֶה לָכֶם כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ־חָג וְשִׂמְחַת לֵבָב כַּהוֹלֵךְ בֶּחָלִיל לָבוֹא בְהַר־יְהֹוָה אֶל־צוּר יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en:
For you, there shall be singing
As on a night when a festival is hallowed;
There shall be rejoicing as when they march
With flute, with hand-drums, and with lyres
To the Rock of Israel on the Mount of GOD.

notes.he: הלל:
notes.en: The song: Hallel.

notes.he: בעשיית מלאכה:
notes.en: Sanctified: with regard to the performance of labor.

notes.he: הלל:
notes.en: Requires song: Hallel.

messages.text: On Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur, which are called an appointed day and also are sanctified with regard to the prohibition against the performance of labor, let us say hallel.
Hallel is not recited on those days due to the statement of Rabbi Abbahu.

The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, for what reason do the Jewish people not recite songs of praise, i.e., hallel, before You on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur?

notes.dh: אמרו מלאכי השרת מפני מה אין ישראל אומרים שירה לפניך בר"ה וביום הכיפורים
notes.he: אבל לא קאמר מפני מה אין אנו אומרים שירה משמע שמלאכי השרת אומרים שירה ולכך אומר ר"י דבר"ה וביום הכיפורים אין לדלג והחיות ישוררו וכרובים יפארו:
notes.en: The ministering angels said: Why do the Jewish people not recite song before You on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur? It does not say “Why do we not recite song,” which implies that the ministering angels do recite song. Therefore Ri says that on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur one should not skip [the line of the liturgy] “And the ḥayyot sing, and the cherubim glorify.”

messages.text: He said to them: Is it possible that while the King is sitting on the throne of judgment and the books of life and the books of death are open before Him, the Jewish people would be reciting joyous songs of praise before Me? Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur are somber days of judgment whose mood is incompatible with the recitation of hallel.
But what about Hanukkah, which has neither this or that, i.e., there is no special offering on it, nor is labor prohibited, and yet one says hallel.

notes.he: לא חלוק בקרבן ולא מקודש לחג ולא אסור בעשיית מלאכה]:
notes.en: Which has neither this nor that: it is neither distinct in its offering, nor sanctified as a festival and forbidden in labor.

messages.text: Hallel is recited on Hanukkah not because of its status as a Festival, but because of the miracle that occurred on those days.
If so, on Purim, when there is also this factor, i.e., a miracle occurred on that day, let us say hallel.
Hallel is not recited on Purim because one does not recite a song of praise for a miracle that occurred outside of Eretz Yisrael.
But there is the exodus from Egypt, which was a miracle that took place outside of Eretz Yisrael, and yet we say hallel on Passover night in commemoration of it?
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objects to this explanation:
messages.quote: one does not recite a song of praise for a miracle that occurred outside of Eretz Yisrael

messages.text: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

Until the Jewish people entered Eretz Yisrael, all lands were deemed fit for songs of praise to be recited for miracles performed within their borders, as all lands were treated equally. But once the Jewish people entered Eretz Yisrael, that land became endowed with greater sanctity, and all the other lands were no longer deemed fit for songs of praise to be recited for miracles performed within them.
The reading of the Megilla, i.e., the Scroll of Esther, is equivalent to reciting hallel.
messages.lead: An alternative answer as to why hallel is not recited on Purim:

notes.he: קריאת המגילה:
notes.en: Its reading: the reading of the Megilla.

messages.text: Granted, hallel is said there, when recalling the exodus from Egypt, as after that salvation one can recite the phrase in hallel: “Give praise, O servants of the Lord”, since after the Israelites’ servitude to Pharaoh ended with their salvation, they were truly servants of the Lord and not servants of Pharaoh. But can it be said here, after the salvation commemorated on Purim: “Give praise, O servants of the Lord,” which would indicate that after the salvation the Jewish people were only servants of the Lord and not servants of Ahasuerus? Not so, as even after the miracle of Purim, we are still the servants of Ahasuerus, since the Jews remained in exile under Persian rule.

verse.he: הַלְלוּ־יָהּ ׀ הַלְלוּ עַבְדֵי יְהֹוָה הַלְלוּ אֶת־שֵׁם יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en:
ש ת Hallelujah.
O servants of GOD, give praise;
praise the name of GOD.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Rav Naḥman, who says that the reading of the Megilla itself is an act of reciting hallel, there is a difficulty: Isn’t it taught in a baraita: Once the Jewish people entered Eretz Yisrael, that land became endowed with greater sanctity, and all the other lands were no longer deemed fit for songs of praise to be recited for miracles performed within them. How, then, may one recite a form of hallel by reading the Megilla?
messages.quote: The reading of the Megilla is equivalent to reciting hallel

messages.text: He maintains that once the people were exiled from Eretz Yisrael, the other lands returned to their initial suitability, and were once again deemed fit for reciting hallel, in commemoration of miracles performed within them.

notes.he: לומר שירה אפי' בחוצה לארץ [מקרא מגילה]:
notes.en: They returned to their initial permission: to recite song even outside the Land [by the reading of the Megilla].

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And one would not play a copper flute [abuv]; rather, one would play a flute [abuv] of reed, because its sound is pleasant. The mishna opens by referring to flutes and calls them ḥalil and then concludes by referring to playing an abuv.
messages.quote: And one would not play with a copper flute

messages.text: A ḥalil is the same as an abuv. Its original name was abuv; and why does the mishna call it a ḥalil? The reason is that its sound is sweet [ḥali].

notes.he: מתוק קולו לשמוע:
notes.en: That its sound is sweet [ḥali]: its sound is sweet to hear.

messages.text: There was a flute in the Temple; it was smooth and it was thin, i.e., its sides were thin; it was made from reed, and it was in existence from the days of Moses. The king issued a command and they plated the flute with gold, but then its sound was not as pleasant as it was previously. They therefore removed its plating and its sound was then as pleasant as it was before.

notes.he: קלוף:
notes.en: Smooth: peeled.

notes.he: טינב"ש. גילדו דקה:
notes.en: Thin: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss); its bark was thin.

messages.text: Similarly, there was a cymbal in the Temple; it was made from copper and its sound was pleasant. It became damaged and the Sages sent for and brought artisans from Alexandria in Egypt and they repaired it, but its sound was not as pleasant as before. They removed the materials with which the cymbal had been repaired and its sound was then as pleasant as it had been before the repair.

notes.he: שני כלים מכין זה ע"ג זה וקולם דק וקורין להן צנב"ש:
notes.en: Cymbal [tziltzal]: two instruments struck one against the other, whose sound is thin; they are called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: קורין צימבש [ציבלי] והן כעין [ב'] גלילי נחושת ומכין זה בזה:
notes.en: Tziltzul [cymbal]: they call them tzimbash [tzibli] (a vernacular gloss), and they are like [two] copper discs that are struck against each other.

messages.text: There was a mortar in the Temple; it was made of copper and it was from the days of Moses, and it was used to compound the spices for the incense. It became damaged and they brought artisans from Alexandria in Egypt and they repaired it, but it did not compound the spices as well as it had before. They removed the materials with which the mortar had been repaired and it then compounded the spices as it had before it was repaired.

notes.he: שבה היו כותשין סממני הקטרת והיה קולה צלול ומפטמת הבשמים יפה ונותנת בהן ריח כדאמרי' בכריתות (דף ו:) השוחק אומר היטב הדק הדק היטב שהקול יפה לבשמים:
notes.en: It would compound the spices: in it they would pound the ingredients of the incense; its sound was clear, and it compounded the spices well and gave them fragrance, as we say in Keritot (6b): the one who grinds says, “Grind thoroughly, thoroughly grind,” because the voice is good for the spices.

notes.he: נותנת ריח טוב בבשמים:
notes.en: It would compound the spices: it gave the spices a good fragrance.

messages.text: These two copper vessels, the cymbal and the mortar, were remnants from the First Temple and they were damaged and they could not be repaired in an effective manner. And it was with regard to the copper vessels constructed for the First Temple that David said: “All these vessels, which Hiram made for King Solomon, in the House of the Lord, were of burnished brass” (I Kings 7:45), and, in a parallel verse, “bright brass” (II Chronicles 4:16).

verse.he: וְאֶת־הַסִּירוֹת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִים וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָקוֹת וְאֵת כׇּל־הַכֵּלִים (האהל) [הָאֵלֶּה] אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה חִירָם לַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה בֵּית יְהֹוָה נְחֹשֶׁת מְמֹרָט׃
verse.en: the pails, the scrapers, and the sprinkling bowls. All those vessels in the House of GOD that Hiram made for King Solomon were of burnished bronze.

notes.he: צלצל ומכתשת נחושת:
notes.en: Two vessels: the cymbal and the copper mortar.

notes.he: דק שיכולין לקפלו:
notes.en: Burnished [memorat]: thin, so that one can fold it.

notes.he: קלל לויישנ"ט:
notes.en: Bright [memorak]: polished (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: פ"ה על נחושת שמוציא בהם מיהו קשה דהאי קרא בעלמא במלכים דכתיב נחשת ממורט ובדברי הימים (ב ד) כתיב נחשת מרוק ומאי קאמר ועליהם אמר דוד ונראה לר"י דה"ג ועליהם אמר קרא נחשת ממורט נחושת (ממורק):
notes.en: And concerning them David said, “burnished brass”: Rashi explained it as about the brass [the rest of his phrase here is unclear]. But it is difficult: this verse is simply in Kings, where “burnished brass” is written, and in Chronicles (II 4) “bright brass” is written; so what does “and concerning them David said” mean? It seems to Ri that the reading is: “and concerning them the verse says, burnished brass, (bright) brass.”

notes.he: מן המשכן:
notes.en: They were remnants from the First Temple: from the Tabernacle.

notes.he: צהוב הרבה:
notes.en: Burnished [memorat]: very yellow.

messages.text: And with regard to these two items it states in the verse describing the vessels that Ezra brought to Jerusalem: “And vessels of fine golden brass, two, precious as gold”.

verse.he: וּכְפֹרֵי זָהָב עֶשְׂרִים לַאֲדַרְכֹנִים אָלֶף וּכְלֵי נְחֹשֶׁת מֻצְהָב טוֹבָה שְׁנַיִם חֲמוּדֹת כַּזָּהָב׃
verse.en: also, twenty gold bowls worth one thousand darics and two vessels of good, shining bronze, as precious as gold.

notes.he: חלק הרבה ואף בימי עזרא היו ועליהן אמר כו':
notes.en: Bright [memorak]: very smooth. And they still existed in the days of Ezra, and concerning them it says, and so on.

messages.text: Rav and Shmuel disagree as to the meaning of the phrase: Two, precious as gold. One said: Each and every one of these brass vessels was as valuable as two vessels made from gold. And the other one said: The two of them together were as valuable as one vessel made from gold.
The two of them together were as valuable as one vessel made from gold.
messages.lead: Similarly, Rav Yosef teaches the following explanation found in a baraita:

messages.text: The cymbals and mortars were pairs, i.e., there were two cymbals and two mortars, as it is stated in the aforementioned verse “two”; do not read it as two [shenayim], but as pairs [sheniyyim].
messages.lead: Another explanation of the verse in Ezra. It is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: שני צלצלים ושני מכתשות:
notes.en: Pairs: two cymbals and two mortars.

notes.he: ב' מכתשות וב' צלצלים]:
notes.en: [They were pairs: two mortars and two cymbals.]

messages.text: The Siloam pool used to spurt forth water through an opening with a diameter like that of an issar coin. The king issued a command and they widened the opening so that its waters would increase, but the waters actually decreased. And they subsequently decreased the size of the opening again and it once again spurted forth water as it had before.
messages.lead: § Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches in a baraita:

notes.he: פי המעיין שהוא נובע שם רחב כאיסר:
notes.en: Like an issar: the mouth of the spring, where it gushes out, was as wide as an issar.

messages.text: All this serves to uphold that which is stated in the verse: “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might”, i.e., man should not think that he can accomplish anything he wishes.

verse.he: כֹּה ׀ אָמַר יְהֹוָה אַל־יִתְהַלֵּל חָכָם בְּחׇכְמָתוֹ וְאַל־יִתְהַלֵּל הַגִּבּוֹר בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ אַל־יִתְהַלֵּל עָשִׁיר בְּעׇשְׁרוֹ׃
verse.en:
Thus said GOD:
Let not the wise glory in their wisdom;
Let not the strong glory in their strength;
Let not the rich glory in their riches.

notes.he: שחכמתו אינה אלא מקלקלת לפי שכלי מקדש ראשון ע"פ הגבורה נעשו דכתיב (ד"ה א כח) הכל בכתב מיד ה' עלי השכיל כל מלאכת התבנית:
notes.en: Let not the wise man glory: for his wisdom only spoils, since the vessels of the First Temple were made by the word of the Almighty, as it is written (I Chronicles 28[:19]): “All this in writing, from the hand of the Lord upon me; He made me understand all the work of the pattern.”

messages.text: There was no hirdolim in the Temple.
messages.lead: And likewise Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say, with regard to the musical instruments in the Temple:

notes.he: הרדווליס בסמ"ך גריס רש"י ונראה לר' הרדוולים במ"ם וכן יש בבראשית רבה ערדולין בעיר ומדינה נהפכה פירוש ערדוולין כמו הרדוולין והם מיני כלי זמר מ"ם מתחלפת בנו"ן הרדוולים זהו תרגום של עוגב:
notes.en: Rashi reads hirdavlis, with a samekh, and it seems to Rabbi [a Tosafist] that it is hirdavlim, with a mem; and so in Bereshit Rabba: “ardavlin in the city, and the province was overturned”; ardavlin is like hirdavlin, and they are kinds of musical instruments, as mem interchanges with nun. Hirdavlim is the Aramaic translation of ugav [an organ].

notes.he: טבלא:
notes.en: Hirdavlis: a board.

messages.text: What is a hirdolim?
messages.quote: There was no hirdolim in the Temple

messages.text: It is a hydraulic organ. It was not used in the Temple because its sound is pleasant but it disrupts the melody.

notes.he: זוג ועינבל שקורים אישקליט"א:
notes.en: Hirdavlis, tavla gurgedana [Rashi’s reading; see Tosafot]: a bell and its clapper, which they call (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: כשהיה קול זה מסיים:
notes.en: And it disrupts the melody: when this sound was ending.

notes.he: קלוגתא (מורגרו בלע"ז). [של אותו מין]:
notes.en: Gudgena [so Rabbeinu Gershom reads]: kloguta (with a vernacular gloss), [of that kind].

notes.he: של שיר:
notes.en: And it disrupts the melody: of the song.

messages.text: There was an instrument called magreifa in the Temple.
messages.lead: Rava bar Sheila said that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said:

notes.he: שבה גורפין את דשן המזבח. וודי"ל והוא כעין כף:
notes.en: Magreifa: with which they rake up the ashes of the altar (Rashi adds an Old French gloss); it is like a scoop.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס שגורפין בה הדשן וקשה דהא היתה כלי זמר אלא נראה לפרש דשני מיני מגריפות היו אחת לדשן ואחת של שיר:
notes.en: There was a magreifa in the Temple: the Kuntres [Rashi] explained it as the one with which they rake up the ashes. But it is difficult, since this one was a musical instrument! Rather, it seems one should explain that there were two kinds of magreifa: one for the ashes and one for song.

notes.he: כלי שבו חתין את האפר מן המזבח:
notes.en: Magreifa: a vessel with which they rake the ashes from the altar.

messages.text: Continues on 11a: what the magreifa was like, with ten holes, each giving many kinds of tone.
